highlights.title: Ofcom launches investigation into Pornhub over its age checks
highlights.summary: The regulator said it had concerns Aylo "may not have conducted sufficient due diligence" over verifying the age of its users.
body: Ofcom has launched an investigation into Pornhub owner, Aylo, over whether the site's new age checks are effectively stopping children from accessing adult content.
The regulator said in May that Pornhub started using a new age verification process for some users, which relies on a third party, in this case Apple.

It said it had concerns that Aylo "may not have conducted sufficient due diligence and testing" before implementing this new process, and so it "may not be highly effective" at preventing children from seeing pornography.
Under the UK's Online Safety Act (OSA), sites that host pornographic material must use highly effective age assurance to ensure whether a user is over 18.

highlights.summary: Most leaders on a trade mission stick to the pitch, but when I interviewed Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis this week, he also admitted that no government is ready for what AI is about to do.
body: Disrupt ticket savings of up to $200 + 50% off a second ends Sept 25, 11:59 p.m. PT. REGISTER HERE.

Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis came to San Francisco on Monday night to promote Greece, but he also did something that heads of state on trade missions don’t typically do. In front of roughly 250 founders, investors and operators, he said openly that he doesn’t have answers to many of the AI questions leaders around the world are more privately debating.

The prime minister, speaking with this editor at an event hosted by Endeavor Greece, the local arm of a global nonprofit that supports entrepreneurs in emerging and growth markets, described his Bay Area trip as partly a fact-finding mission. He’d spent the morning touring Tesla and Sequoia Capital, among other stops, with plans to head this week to the U.N. General Assembly in New York. But the trip was also meant to build bridges; indeed, he was pitching anyone in tech who might consider setting up shop in Greece, which is set to regain developed market status next year from MSCI, the influential index provider.

highlights.title: The Italian Job gets a sequel! Can Mancini inspire a new generation?
highlights.summary: This year, Italian football fell to its lowest ebb. In Europe, no Italian club made it past the quarter-finals - while Atalanta were the only Serie A side to reach the Champions League last 16. But that was nothing compared to the national team.
body: Roberto Mancini is back as Italy head coach after a second spell; the former Man City boss won Euro 2020 with the Azzurri, who have not qualified for the last three World Cups; With exclusive insight from Gianluigi Donnarumma, Sky Sports' Sam Blitz analyses the road back for Italy...
Italy did not qualify for the third World Cup in a row. An unthinkable prospect given they have won the competition four times.
The first two failures to qualify were masked over by the Euro 2020 triumph at Wembley. That at least gave the nation hope.

The third World Cup failure was one last straw. A 48-team World Cup did not include Italy. It brought about the resignations of not just head coach Gennaro Gattuso, but also Italian FA president Gabriele Gravina and Gianluigi Buffon as the team's head of delegation.

highlights.title: State of Decay studio Undead Labs goes independent after Xbox restructuring, but lays off "a significant number" of the team in doing so
highlights.summary: State of Decay studio Undead Labs has shared good and bad news following Xbox's second round of job cuts this year.
body: The good news is that Undead Labs, owned by Microsoft since 2018, has gone independent and is worker-owned as well, the studio said in a statement on its website. The bad news is that the studio is laying off "a significant number" of staff in doing so, the company added on LinkedIn.

"Independence brings us closer to our community and lets us focus on what matters most: making the best games we can and earning the continued support of the people who choose to spend their time with us," Undead Labs studio head Philip Holt said in the website statement.

"Unfortunately," Undead Labs added on LinkedIn, "today we are also saying goodbye to a significant number of our colleagues. It's difficult to reach this moment knowing that not everyone who helped get us here gets to make the rest of the journey with us.
"There have been far too many announcements like this across the industry, and we hate adding to that list. These are people we'd hire again in a heartbeat, and we hope the industry takes notice."

highlights.title: Better prompt caching for GPT-6
highlights.summary: Learn how GPT-6 improves prompt caching with higher cache hit rates, new diagnostics, explicit breakpoints, and controls that reduce latency and costs.
body: Higher cache hit rates and new tools to help persistent agents run faster and cost less.

GPT‑6 enables persistent agents to work for hours on complex tasks, from refactoring codebases to producing well-researched documents and presentations. The applications behind these agents make a series of API requests that build on one another, often carrying forward the same instructions, tool definitions, and context from earlier turns. OpenAI caches that shared context to reuse computation across requests, reducing response times and giving developers discounts of up to 90% on cached input tokens.

With the GPT‑6 family, we launched an improved prompt caching system that delivers higher cache hit rates by default. We now give cache discounts for eligible shared prefixes reused within a 30-minute window. We’re also introducing new tools to help developers monitor cache performance, diagnose misses, and choose how much of a prompt to cache.

highlights.title: Can Europe inspire new 'Medinah miracle' at Presidents Cup?
highlights.summary: If the International Team are going to end Team USA’s Presidents Cup dominance this week, live on Sky Sports, they may require their own 'Miracle at Medinah' to do it.
body: Fourteen years on from Team Europe producing a historic final-day comeback to claim Ryder Cup glory at the same venue, Geoff Ogilvy sees his side head in as heavy underdogs to avoid an 11th consecutive Presidents Cup defeat.

The United States have won every edition since 2005 and only been beaten once in the event's history, before seven of the 24 players involved in this year's contest were even born, with all logic pointing to that run continuing in Illinois.

Nothing less than victory will be acceptable for Team USA, 12 months on from a humbling home Ryder Cup loss where only a singles fightback prevented a heavier defeat, with Brandt Snedeker aware of the expectation to deliver.
"It's the elephant in the room you have to address," Snedeker said. "Just because these last (Presidents Cup) teams have been successful, doesn't mean we're going to be successful.

highlights.title: 5 Perfect 'Peanuts' Comics From 1950s That Prove Charles Schulz Is a Genius
highlights.summary: But while Schulz was still figuring out the look and feel of Peanuts back in the 1950s, the early years contained sparks of absolute genius that would inform the strip’s 50-year run.
body: In the early days of Charles Schulz’s Peanuts comics, the characters looked quite a bit different. They were smaller, rounder, and a bit more “cutesy.” The comic strip debuted on Oct. 2, 1950 and over the first decade of drawing the characters, Schulz found their distinct look, which was still cute, but with far more personality for each character, allowing you to tell them apart more easily.

The very first Peanuts comic contains the now-forgotten characters of Shermy and Patty (not Peppermint Patty, another girl named just Patty). The two of them are sitting while Shermy goes on about Charlie Brown. “Well! Here comes ol’ Charlie Brown!” he says in the first strip as Charlie Brown approaches in the distance. “Good ol’ Charlie Brown… Yes, sir!” says Shermy as Charlie Brown passes by. “Good ol’ Charlie Brown…” Shermy trails off as Charlie Brown is still in earshot. Then, once Charlie Brown is far enough away, Shermy lets his true feelings be known by saying “How I hate him!”

highlights.summary: William and Catherine renew their friendship with the Hollywood star at the premiere for his film Digger.
body: The Prince and Princess of Wales renewed their friendship with Tom Cruise at the premiere of the Hollywood star's latest film in London on Tuesday.
Cruise took the hand of Catherine, Princess of Wales, as they talked and laughed on a black carpet - instead of the traditional red - before the royal gala screening of Digger in Leicester Square.
Cruise has known the prince and princess for a number of years and also met William's mother, Princess Diana, and attended her funeral in 1997.
Catherine wore a pair of Diana's pearl drop earrings to the premiere on Tuesday, as well as the late Queen Mother's amethyst sautoir necklace.

highlights.title: From 50p gold hot pants to Paul Smith suits: how Kylie Minogue became one of pop’s ultimate chameleons
highlights.summary: The star’s rise from Ramsay Street to global superstar is the subject of a new book. It’s a journey that has cleverly harnessed the power of fashion to transform, subvert – and shock. On 20 December 1989, Kylie Minogue first harnessed the power of fashion.
body: Before then, there’d been her Neighbours character Charlene’s peak-80s silk taffeta and lace wedding dress, and Kylie the pop star on the cover of her first album, in 1988, wearing a topless hat showing off cascading curls. But that had been fashion forced on her, at a time when she had no say in her image.

From that moment, Kylie, or the public-facing version at least, took control. She used fashion as a reflection of her desire and need to evolve. Forever the pop chameleon, she anchored each new era via deliberate fashion choices that communicated where she was at in her life and career. As Jean Paul Gaultier wrote in the foreword to her 2012 photo-book Kylie/Fashion: “You change, you transform yourself, you adapt with the evolution of times, fashions, desires … and still stay yourself.”

highlights.title: Rabbit’s new AI agent doesn’t need an R1 to run
highlights.summary: Rabbit, the company behind the underwhelming R1 device, is rolling out a standalone AI agent that you don't need its hardware to use, as reported earlier by Wired. The startup says its new OS3 "agentic operating system" runs in the cloud but operates locally across Windows, Mac, and Linux devices.
body: According to Rabbit, you can add up to five devices to one account, along with your preferred AI models. OS3 will automatically determine the devices, files, apps, and AI models it needs to complete a task. You can also access OS3 through its dedicated desktop site, a paired messaging app like Telegram or iMessage, as well as on Rabbit’s R1 device.

Though Rabbit founder Jesse Lyu tells Wired that the startup has stopped manufacturing R1 devices, it isn’t giving up on AI hardware entirely. It’s instead focusing on a new vibe-coding “cyberdeck” that will run OS3 when it launches within “months,” Wired reports.

Rabbit claims its OS3 system won’t store, copy, use, or sell your data. It notes that it will still keep your chats and memories stemming from them on its servers. Other AI providers linked to OS3 will also handle your data under their own privacy rules.
Sign in to see your notifications or create an account to join the conversation.

highlights.title: New UK agency to fight ‘information warfare’ from likes of Russia, Burnham tells UN
highlights.summary: PM aims to ‘stem poisonous tide’ of disinformation and deepfakes with National Centre for Information Defence. Security chiefs will set up a new national centre to tackle disinformation and deepfakes from hostile states such as Russia, Andy Burnham has announced, saying the government had a duty to…
body: The National Centre for Information Defence will “detect, attribute and disrupt” information attacks by foreign powers, many of which are enabled by AI, bringing together the intelligence agencies, law enforcement and social media companies.

It will be tasked with making sure the UK has the defensive capability necessary to combat information warfare and build national resilience by helping communities to identify and combat disinformation, preventing a “distorted and untrue” narrative about the UK.

Burnham said the country would have to go into the next decade “eyes wide open” about “insidious” campaigns, many of which had been orchestrated by Russia, which “twisted” what people at home felt about their own country and community.

In eye-catching remarks, the prime minister suggested that Britons who were struggling with the cost of living and young people not in education, training or employment may be particularly susceptible to foreign influence online, underlining how inequality further undermined society.

highlights.title: 32 Years Ago, a Crucial 'X-Files' Episode Introduced the Show’s Best Monster Ever
highlights.summary: The term “monster” is used liberally, mind you, because here it could refer to any weird new creature, case, or even superpowered person. Regardless, there were a lot of different monsters on the show, but all of them fall short of one the show introduced during a season 2 episode called “The Host.”
body: “The Host” was the second episode of season 2. It takes place during a period when the X-Files division of the FBI has been shut down. Mulder is sent on a case involving a waterlogged body found in the Newark, NJ sewer system, and he is convinced it's a punishment from his bosses at the FBI. Over the course of the investigation, however, he finds out that this is, indeed, an X-File.

When Agent Scully performs an autopsy on the body, she finds a flukeworm in its liver. Soon after, a city sanitation worker is attacked in the sewer system by what he believes to be a python, but the giant bite mark on his back matches the mouth of a flukeworm, although much, much larger. After the sanitation worker dies, Mulder visits the sewage treatment plant, which has accidentally captured a creature that has the size and shape of a man, but with the face and mouth of a flukeworm. Soon after, the Flukeman, as the creature comes to be known, begins attacking workers at the sanitation plant in an effort to escape.

highlights.title: A moment that changed me: my brother gave me an unexpected gift – and a whole new life at sea
highlights.summary: The water was my childhood playground but, as I grew up, my health left me landbound. Then my brother found a way to launch me back into the waves... My brother and I grew up surfing at Porthcawl in south Wales.
body: I was in my teens when I started to develop chronic illnesses, including endometriosis. At first, I was still able to surf – I just needed to rest afterwards. Then, in my early 20s, I developed further chronic conditions, including a connective tissue disorder that affected my joints and muscle strength. I could stand just for a few seconds and was able to walk only a few metres. At 23, an acute infection led to complications, including the loss of the use of my legs. Later, my stomach became paralysed; I’m now fed via a tube that runs down my oesophagus, through my stomach and into my intestines.

When I was 24, one year after becoming a full-time wheelchair user, my brother, Leon, gave me an unexpected birthday gift: a battered, pink and yellow surfboard to which he had fitted shower handles either side of where my chest would rest. He was training as an adaptive surf coach, he explained, so that he could teach me.

At a time when every day seemed like a riptide threatening to drag me into another hospital admission, the new surfboard felt like an ambitious gift. But it also sparked a desire to adapt and take risks again. It was crying out for the sea.

highlights.title: Poitras Center to fuel early careers of 50 young scientists dedicated to psychiatric disorders research
highlights.summary: Patricia and James Poitras ’63 provide fellowships for graduate students and postdocs who will shape the future of mental health research.
body: Patricia and James Poitras ’63, longtime MIT supporters, have launched a fellowship program for graduate students and postdocs studying major mental illness, expanding their MIT philanthropy to directly support early-career scientists. The commitment establishes 50 two-year fellowships through the Poitras Center for Psychiatric Disorders Research at MIT’s McGovern Institute for Brain Research. Five fellowships will be awarded every year for the next decade, creating a long-term talent pipeline focused specifically on psychiatric disorders.

The $10 million gift is the latest in a series of philanthropic investments from the Poitras family to strengthen MIT’s capacity to address the growing burden of severe depression and anxiety, bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, and other complex psychiatric conditions. “Pat and Jim have remained steadfast in their decades-long commitment to bold research that can transform mental wellness,” says Robert Desimone, director of the McGovern Institute and head of the Poitras Center. “Their remarkable support of rising talent in the MIT ecosystem is yet another emblem of their commitment to that cause.”

highlights.summary: Head coach Dan McFarland is excited to have the backing of Newcastle Red Bulls' owners as he tries to fuse a new team together in the Prem this season.
body: It is all change at Newcastle Red Bulls as they prepare for the new Prem season, but they plan to tackle it with the sort of fearless approach for which their owners are renowned.
With Red Bull taking over at Kingston Park in August 2025, it was a scramble to get things in place for last season.
As a result, Newcastle could not bridge the gap to the other nine teams and finished bottom for a fourth successive campaign, with just two wins in 18 games.

But, after a huge influx of players in the summer, 'Red Bulls 2.0' under new head coach Dan McFarland are ready to embrace the challenge as they begin with a daunting trip to champions Northampton Saints on Friday night.
points: Head coach Dan McFarland is excited to have the backing of Newcastle Red Bulls' owners as he tries to fuse a new team together in the Prem this season.

highlights.title: Esports tournaments do it better in person
highlights.summary: Jacob got his hands on a gaming PC for the first time when he was about 12 years old. He swiftly realised the local PC repair store had ripped him off with his build and vowed never to let another soul build his rig again. With this vow, Jacob the hardware junkie was born.
body: I'm currently at Logitech G Play in Warsaw where a Counter-Strike 2 tournament is being held. As someone who properly got into Counter-Strike when CS:GO launched way back when, I can see things have changed quite a bit. Back then, we struggled with janky spectator cams; now, we have on-stage lighting that starts when the bomb is planted and speeds up in time with it. Things like this, and the boomy theatre bass, have left me incredibly impressed with the IRL tournament experience.

highlights.title: Byron Bay’s ‘daggier neighbour’ named in Lonely Planet’s 2027 Best in Travel list
highlights.summary: The Tweed region is easily as beautiful as nearby Byron, but without the glamour and crowds. For locals, the biggest drawcard is the community. Locals in the Tweed region already knew we were a bit special, obviously. The sheer beauty of the place routinely stops you in your tracks.
body: Now those who came here to escape the world may find it is coming to them.
“Bloody hell,” says a fellow resident Sarah Killington, whose verandah overlooks the wide, flat Tweed Valley. “We don’t want to turn into another Gold Coast.”

Jessica Lockhard, Lonely Planet’s destination editor for Oceania, says that the Tweed was chosen because: “What we’re really looking for is places that feel less crowded, that are offering a deeper and more meaningful experience, or are really inviting travellers to slow down.” We can definitely do slow.

Tweed Shire is Byron Shire adjacent, easily as beautiful but without the glamour. There are fewer “healers” and drum circles, less tourist overcrowding and recently arrived wealth. We are traditionally the poorer, daggier neighbour. And we like it that way. A place that people usually drive past on their way from the Gold Coast to Byron Bay. You can almost feel the atmosphere change when you enter Byron.

highlights.title: OpenAI wants to consult elite mathematicians about how to not fumble again
highlights.summary: After turning a string of spectacular mathematical results into a reputational crisis, OpenAI is consulting human mathematicians to help it figure out a less disastrous path forward.
body: ‘The group will advise on the review and communication of emerging results.’

On Monday, the company announced a new independent panel of mathematicians tasked with advising it and other AI companies on their interactions with mathematical research and the wider mathematics community, including how new results are presented and released. Its abrupt arrival caught many mathematicians by surprise. Researchers told The Verge the group is a good first step, but many said they were left with basic questions about what it will actually do, how much influence it will have, and whether OpenAI will actually listen to it, as well as concerns over whether such a small group of prominent researchers can represent the wider mathematical community.

highlights.title: How to Claim Your Cut of Apple’s $250 Million Siri Settlement
highlights.summary: Apple may pay out up to $95 for each eligible iPhone purchased by someone who felt misled about Siri’s release. You have until December 21 to submit a claim.
body: In May, Apple agreed to pay out $250 million as part of a class action lawsuit over claims the company overhyped its Apple Intelligence tools, specifically the long-delayed Siri AI overhaul.

Although the revamped Siri AI voice assistant is now available for owners of newer iPhones via iOS 27, you may still be eligible to claim cash back for past purchases. This settlement covers customers in the US who made their purchases from June 10, 2024 to March 29, 2025, and bought certain iPhone 15 or iPhone 16 models from Apple. If you qualify, you might receive up to $95 for each phone.

This settlement revolves around Apple’s promotion of Siri features to sell iPhones. “I expected to receive a Siri Apple Intelligence feature and did not receive it,” reads part of the statement you have to sign when filling out the claim form. As part of the settlement, Apple denies any wrongdoing.
“We resolved this matter to stay focused on doing what we do best, delivering the most innovative products and services to our users,” read part of Apple’s statement from May about the settlement.
points: Apple may pay out up to $95 for each eligible iPhone purchased by someone who felt misled about Siri’s release.
You have until December 21 to submit a claim.

highlights.title: Brothers Season 1 Review
highlights.summary: Brothers Season 1 review: Well, at least Woody and Matthew are having fun together…
body: The first two episodes of Brothers debut on Apple TV on September 23.

Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson are great actors, and the last time they made a series together — the first season of True Detective — it was a triumph. It sure is nice to know that they’re such good friends in real life (friends are great!), but Apple TV’s attempt to capitalize on all of this history via their on-screen reunion in Brothers is a misguided endeavor.

In the new series, McConaughey and Harrelson play themselves, kicking off with Woody and his family going to visit Matthew and his family in Texas. The big hook here — based on something the actors have in fact theorized as a possibility in real life — is that in this fictionalized version of these two celebrities’ lives, Woody discovers he and Matthew might be biological half-brothers thanks to an offhand comment from Matthew’s mom (Holland Taylor).

highlights.summary: Diver Peter van Rodijnen’s footage of basking whales, plankton blooms and fatherly fish disputes the idea that the North Sea is a bleak wilderness. The North Sea, with its cold grey waters, is the world’s drabbest.

He also brings us cute, coo-worthy stories from the depths; take the male shorthorn sculpin fish (no looker, it must be said) who spends the winter looking after his eggs, cleaning and blowing fresh water over them. Van Rodijnen’s camera is there for the baby fish hatching – pop, pop, pop out of their pearly plump pink eggs. There are some quirky stories, too, including a barnacle with a superlong penis.

highlights.title: Woman's brain worm infection confirmed after eggs grow tails in lab test
highlights.summary: Out of nowhere, a woman's right arm and leg started shaking uncontrollably. In the moments leading up to the experience, she seemed well; she had no headache, confusion, or weakness. But for about a minute, half of her body juddered.
body: The woman, a rice farmer in the Philippines, headed to the emergency department. There, doctors gave her a physical exam and found nothing out of the ordinary. Then they took a look at her brain. Magnetic resonance imaging revealed a bright cluster of nodules surrounded by fluid in her left frontal lobe. The doctors had an immediate guess as to what they were: worm eggs.

In a case report published in the latest issue of the New England Journal of Medicine, doctors write that they suspected the woman had neuroschistosomiasis, an uncommon complication of an infection with a Schistosoma parasitic worm, aka a blood fluke. In the Philippines, the most common fluke is S. japonicum. It's also found in China and part of Indonesia; despite its name, it has been eliminated from Japan.

highlights.title: Introducing GPT-6 Sol and Luna
highlights.summary: Meet GPT-6 Sol and Luna, two models that bring frontier intelligence to everyday work with different balances of capability and cost.
body: More ways to bring frontier intelligence into the work you do every day.

Earlier this month, we introduced GPT‑6 Astra, the most intelligent and aligned model in the world. While the most demanding and important projects still call for Astra’s full depth, work happens at different scales, rhythms, and budgets.

That’s why we’re expanding the GPT‑6 universe with GPT‑6 Sol and GPT‑6 Luna. GPT‑6 Astra introduced a new generation of intelligence—these models help distribute the benefits of that intelligence by advancing the frontier on cost efficiency. We trained GPT‑6 Sol and Luna with similar methods as GPT‑6 Astra, bringing the advances behind Astra’s state-of-the-art performance in professional work, factuality, coding, computer use, and alignment to faster, more affordable models.

highlights.title: Gears of War: E-Day Story Director Laid Off Just a Week Before Early Access Launch
highlights.summary: Gears of War: E-Day's story director has been laid off, just one week before the game's early access launch. Earlier today, Microsoft continued its ongoing reset of the Xbox brand, resulting in 268 staff members losing their jobs across a number of studios.
body: The news comes at a pretty brutal time, as Vaca just publicly celebrated the game going gold last week, and the title will enter early access next week, five days before its global launch. It's unclear what Microsoft is planning to do with The Coalition after Gears of War: E-Day's launch, but cutting key talent doesn't inspire a lot of confidence.

This isn't the only oddly-timed layoff, either. Halo Studios' cinematic director Josh Daniels was also laid off, just one day after getting a promotion. Halo Studios' fate is a lot clearer, however. Activision is taking charge on the future of Halo, while Halo Studios is being gutted. A small team will remain on to support existing Halo games, but a new team is being built under Activision to develop the next mainline game in the franchise.

Gears of War's future hasn't been outlined much by Microsoft. When E-Day was announced years ago, it was suggested that the team would eventually return to the ongoing storyline that was left hanging at the end of Gears 5. However, it's unclear if that's still in the cards with all of the changes happening at Xbox.
points: Gears of War: E-Day's story director has been laid off, just one week before the game's early access launch.
Earlier today, Microsoft continued its ongoing reset of the Xbox brand, resulting in 268 staff members losing their jobs across a number of studios.
